A1.justification: Both complete PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, figures, tables, prompts, limitations, and ethics appendices are readable and support comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix A report original experiments on HumanEval, CIAR, CommonMT, and FairEval, including error injection, resilience analyses, and defense results.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B report original benchmark experiments, expanded defense comparisons, and an analysis of 80 injected coding errors.

M1.justification: V3 introduces concurrent use of Challenger and Inspector as the C+I configuration in Section 5. This is a limited extension combining existing components; AutoTransform, AutoInject, and the individual defense procedures and prompts remain substantively unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four datasets and tasks, including Chinese-to-English translation. Extending MetaGPT to retained tasks changes comparator participation, while the broader 'faulty agents' framing does not establish evaluation on a new population or natural-error scenario.

E2.justification: MetaGPT joins the non-code task comparisons: v2 Appendix B identifies only Camel, MAD, and AgentVerse as extended beyond coding, whereas v3 Table 1 and Appendix C include MetaGPT on all four tasks. The six named systems and single-agent references otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Reported agent counts change from 2–5 to 3 for Self-collab and from 3 to 2–5 for SPP. These are stated setting revisions without evidence establishing reruns. V3 also adds defense controls without injected errors and tests defenses against AutoTransform; v2's defense experiment covered AutoInject.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix A adds an audit classifying 80 AutoInject errors into seven categories. Table 3 adds component-combination comparisons and clean-input controls for the defenses. Existing case studies, role and communication-round analyses, and error-rate sweeps remain; the Pm = 1.0 sweep already appeared in v2 Table 3.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new error-category counts provide descriptive analysis without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Central structure aggregates are substantially revised. For GPT-3.5 hierarchical systems, vanilla/AutoTransform/AutoInject scores change from 67.40/52.15/51.50 in v2 Table 1 to 53.00/46.57/48.12 in v3 Table 5. V3 adds joint-defense and AutoTransform-defense results and changes MAD's semantic-error coding entry from 75.70 to 53.70. Task plots also change although the corresponding quantitative table remains unchanged. Interpretation is limited by changed comparator participation and inconsistent v3 summaries.

T1.justification: The structural categories and Pm/Pe definitions remain equivalent, and neither version presents formal theorems or proofs. Omission of the elementary recovery-rate formula from the defense table removes explanatory documentation without establishing a changed mathematical definition.

C1.justification: V3 broadens the stated focus from malicious agents to faulty agents encompassing clumsy and malicious behavior, and promotes the combined defense as the strongest configuration. The central contributions concerning structural resilience, task sensitivity, error introduction, and correction mechanisms remain.

C2.justification: V3 qualifies the relative effectiveness of AutoTransform and AutoInject by backbone, attributing AutoTransform's greater impact on GPT-4o to stronger instruction following. Appendix A newly argues that diverse injected-error categories make the assessment representative. The existing limitations and most mechanism explanations remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly states AutoInject defaults of Pm = 1.0, Pe = 0.2, and semantic errors, adds a system/role inventory, and supplies MetaGPT Engineer/Reviewer prompts. It omits v2's explicit final-message exclusion and recovery-rate formula; this does not establish procedural changes. The code/data link and existing method prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds citations concerning Internet of Agents, conversational task-solving, scaling collaboration, OASIS, adversarial agent infection, and GPTSwarm. These modestly extend the context while retaining the existing positioning against safety-focused attacks and debate studies. Publication and title updates to retained references do not constitute additional works.

P1.justification: The title and terminology change, the introduction reorganizes its findings, and the former 'Other Factors' material moves into the case-study section. Appendices are reorganized around error analysis, quantitative results, and prompts. Most methodological prose, prompts, and limitations remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from one-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. GPT-4o plots move into the main text and plots are regrouped by backbone. Defense and beneficial-error displays become tables, role/round plots become prose, and new system-detail and error-category tables are added.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful defense controls, an error audit, and MetaGPT prompts, and corrects MAD's semantic-error entry. However, v2's 39.15 error-rate average becomes 48.44 in v3 Table 7 despite component scores averaging about 39.15. V3 Figure 4b also plots GPT-4o AutoTransform coding below 60 while Table 6 retains 73.78. These new, unreconciled reporting problems affect central evidence, leaving the net benefit of the added validation and documentation uncertain.
